xGBoost planet_rank 0.08 is well below median planet but scorer likely penalised low SNR 10.35 and M-dwarf context not EB signatures
dossier.public_summary: A 1.999-hour flat-bottomed 1% dip repeats every 13.8 days with no odd/even or secondary eclipse and a transit duration that matches the small M-dwarf star, implying a 3.7 Earth-radius planet-sized body. The signal is steady across all TESS sectors and individual transits. The on-target location cannot yet be confirmed with difference images, which leaves a faint nearby star that could mimic the dip as an open question that needs ground-based time-series to rule out.

reasons.why: Planet-sized, well below 10 R_earth, with flat-bottom shape (shape.v_sigma -3.724) favouring planet over grazing binary.
Observed 1.999 h duration matches central 2.059 h expectation (stellar_radius duration_ratio 0.97 TIC, 0.93 FLAME, 0.9 GSP-Phot) and fit_log_density_ratio -0.3144, consistent with star density.
No odd/even difference and secondary.snr 3.244 below 5 threshold with best_brightening 3.179 comparable, no stellar secondary.
Depth steady across sectors (sector_depths_by_source verdict steady, TESS-SPOC p 0.874) and transit_depths p_consistent 0.3746, ruling out systematic depth changes.

Centroid inconclusive with no clear difference image, but neighbours.plausible_within_1px 1 requires 0.2248 eclipse; planet interpretation remains best despite low xgboost.planet_rank 0.08, as flat-bottom, density-consistent, steady signal with no binary signs outweighs blended-EB alternative that is not located.
